description: Area of lung tissue filled with fluid, pus, blood, or cells instead of air. Appears as dense opacity on chest X-ray with air bronchograms

criteria: Moderate respiratory distress (RR elevated, mild hypoxia)
moderate.label: Severe pneumonia with consolidation — inpatient

criteria: Sepsis signs (tachycardia, hypotension, altered mental status)
severe.label: Critical — ICU / urgent referral

differential_diagnosis.clues: Acute onset, fever, productive cough, focal consolidation
Chronic cough >2 weeks, weight loss, night sweats, upper lobe predominance, cavitation
differential_diagnosis.prevalence: Very common in endemic areas — always consider

differential_diagnosis.clues: Persistent consolidation not responding to antibiotics, mass lesion, lymphadenopathy
differential_diagnosis.prevalence: Consider if no improvement after 6 weeks of treatment

differential_diagnosis.clues: History of altered consciousness, dysphagia, right lower lobe involvement

if_tb_suspected.note: Do NOT start empiric TB treatment without microbiological evidence unless critically ill

actions: Blood cultures before antibiotics if possible
Consider ICU if mechanical ventilation needed
CT chest if available and not responding to treatment

within_1_week: Non-resolving consolidation after 7 days antibiotics (rule out TB/malignancy)
Need for CT chest or bronchoscopy

tb_screening_note: In areas with high TB prevalence, ANY consolidation persisting >2 weeks should trigger TB workup: sputum GeneXpert (preferred), smear microscopy, or chest X-ray follow-up. This is especially critical in HIV-positive patients where presentation may be atypical.
